title: Yelp Migrates Cassandra to EKS by Moving EBS Volumes
gist: Yelp migrated about 90 production Cassandra clusters (~1,000 pods, ~1,000 TiB) from self-managed Kubernetes to Amazon EKS with zero downtime by re-pointing AZ-bound EBS volumes to new pods (a 'Rolling PV Transplant') instead of streaming data, with one engineer completing the rollout in about three weeks using a Claude-generated bash script. The article contrasts this with Monday.com's streaming-based approach and stresses auditing backups, IAM roles, repair state and alert severity as part of any migration.

insights.claim: Yelp moved about 90 production Cassandra clusters from legacy self-managed Kubernetes to Amazon EKS with zero customer downtime and no data loss by re-pointing existing EBS volumes to new pods instead of streaming data; its largest 54-pod cluster took about 12 hours.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Shows stateful databases can be moved onto managed Kubernetes cheaply, lowering a barrier to EKS adoption.
insights.locator: Yelp has moved its Cassandra fleet

insights.claim: Yelp's technique works because an EBS volume is bound to an Availability Zone rather than to a Kubernetes cluster, and a PersistentVolume is effectively a pointer to a volume ID, so pods can be deleted one at a time on the old cluster and claimed by pre-created EKS pods with the same data and token range.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: A reusable pattern for any AZ-pinned stateful workload, including Kafka, which Yelp also migrated this way.

insights.claim: Yelp rejected the standard approach of adding nodes in the new cluster and streaming data because it would temporarily double compute, incur data transfer costs, and take weeks for the largest clusters.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Avoided double-running capacity and transfer fees represent concrete cloud-cost savings in migrations.
insights.locator: Yelp had already moved its stateless

insights.claim: Across roughly 1,000 pods, about 1,000 TiB moved by pointer rather than over the network, and because no node left the ring, rollback was the same operation in reverse and restored pods within minutes when used.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Cheap rollback lowers migration risk, making similar moves more likely to be approved.

insights.claim: After two weeks of manual and automated dev runs, a single Yelp engineer ran the production rollout in about three weeks, migrating three to six clusters on a typical day.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Automation compresses large infrastructure migrations into small-team efforts.

insights.claim: Yelp had Claude generate its roughly 800-line bash orchestration script from a validated manual runbook rather than asking it to design the procedure, and the script needed only minor adjustments after two days of testing.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Shows a practical pattern for LLM use in operations: humans design and validate, AI codifies.

insights.claim: The one transplant-specific failure at Yelp was a stale VolumeAttachment object left by the AWS CSI controller that silently left EKS pods Pending, leading Yelp to advise explicit timeouts for stalled detach and attach operations.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Silent failures in cloud storage controllers are an operational risk to monitor.

insights.claim: Yelp's backups failed with IAM AccessDenied errors for 48 hours after migration because a new -eks role was not assumed by scheduled jobs, and the alert only filed a ticket instead of paging.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Migrations frequently break backup and identity plumbing; alerting severity matters.

insights.claim: Pausing Cassandra repairs for the migration revealed one Yelp cluster whose repairs had been silently disabled for three months, leaving accumulated data inconsistencies.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Migrations double as audits that expose latent data-integrity issues.

insights.claim: Monday.com migrated K8ssandra-managed Cassandra between EKS clusters by adding new datacenters and streaming data before removing old ones, a model that keeps the old environment intact but requires longer migrations and running both sides at once.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Choice between pointer-swap and streaming trades cost and speed against independence from EBS AZ-binding.

insights.claim: Teams planning a Cassandra migration by either approach should treat verifying backups, monitoring, dashboards, alerts, repair state and IAM roles as part of the migration plan rather than post-migration cleanup.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Operational readiness checks determine migration success more than data-movement mechanics.
